Research Note: #PBFintechLimited (#Policybazaar)

1. Company Overview
PB Fintech Ltd (NSE: #POLICYBZR ) is India’s largest online insurance and credit marketplace. Its flagship platforms are:
- #Policybazaar – Insurance comparison & distribution (core business)
- #Paisabazaar ** – Credit marketplace (personal loans, credit cards, etc.)
- #PBPartners – Tech-enabled network of independent agents/advisors (offline reach into Bharat)
- Newer verticals: Corporate insurance, Reinsurance broking, PB UAE, Pensionbazaar, PB Wheels, Account Aggregator (PB Money)

Mission: Help the Indian middle class deal with Death, Disease and Disability (the 3Ds).

As of June 2026:
- 158.9 million registered consumers
- 28.1 million transacting consumers
- 71.6 million policies sold till date

2. Business Model & Unit Economics
Revenue Streams:
- Commissions / brokerage from insurers on new business
- High-margin renewal / trail income (sticky, ~80% margins)
- Credit marketplace fees
- New initiatives (PB Partners, Corporate, UAE, etc.)

Key Strengths:
- Dominant online market share (>90% of online insurance policies sold historically)
- Strong shift toward **protection products** (Health + Term) — now >70% of core online revenue
- Renewal ARR has compounded strongly (₹935 Cr in FY26, ~80% margins)
- Asset-light model with high operating leverage once scale is achieved

3. Financial Performance Snapshot
 Full Year (April 2025 – March 2026)
The company made ₹6,794 crore in total revenue. This is 37% higher than the previous year.
Insurance business grew strongly — total premium collected reached ₹29,934 crore (up 42%).
Profit almost doubled to ₹670 crore.
The company is now clearly profitable and margins are improving.

Latest Quarter (April – June 2026)
Revenue: ₹1,888 crore (up 40% from the same quarter last year).
Insurance premium: ₹8,372 crore (up 41%).
Profit: ₹163 crore (almost double compared to last year).
Profit margin improved from 6% to 9%.

Highlights:
- Profitability turned consistently positive from FY24 onwards.
- Management is on track for ~₹1,000 Cr PAT in FY27.
- Contribution margins in core online business remain healthy (~42–44%).
- Loan disbursals (Paisabazaar) also growing well (₹30,740 Cr in FY26; +33% in Q1 FY27 core online).

4. Segment Insights

#Policybazaar (Core Online):
- Health insurance market share of 
fresh retail business has risen sharply to ~18–20% (from ~4.5% in FY22).
- Protection products driving quality growth.
- Renewal income is the compounding engine.

PB Partners:
- Expanding rapidly into Tier 2–5 cities via 450k+ partners.
- Market share gains visible; lead over next player widening.

#Paisabazaar :
- Recovering and turning EBITDA positive.
- Expanding into mutual funds & bonds.

International (UAE):
- Became profitable in FY26; premium growth strong (~54% YoY).

5. Competitive Landscape
#Policybazaar remains the clear leader in digital insurance distribution in India. Key competitors include:
- InsuranceDekho (post RenewBuy merger — stronger challenger)
- Turtlemint
- Coverfox / others

Digital still forms a small portion of overall Indian insurance distribution (traditional agency + bancassurance dominate). This leaves significant runway if digital penetration rises.

6. Growth Drivers
1. Under-penetration of insurance in India (especially protection products).
2. Rising health insurance awareness + GST benefits earlier.
3. Shift from pure comparison to full-stack “phygital” (digital + offline partners).
4. High-margin renewals compounding.
5. Credit marketplace recovery + cross-sell.
6. New initiatives (Corporate, Reinsurance, UAE, Pension, etc.) providing optionality.

Management guidance: Sustain ~30% premium growth trajectory.

🚨 INSURANCE STOCKS ARE FALLING 🚨

“ HERE’S WHAT JUST HAPPENED” 

If you saw Policybazaar, insurers, banks & NBFC stocks falling today, this is the simple reason 👇

IRDAI has proposed a major change in how insurance is sold and how much distributors can earn.

⚠️ Important: These are proposals, NOT final rules yet.
Comments are open until 25 October 2026, with implementation expected from FY28 through a phased approach.

🧵 WHAT IS IRDAI TRYING TO CHANGE?

Think of it like this:

Today, insurance distributors can earn significant commissions for selling policies.

IRDAI is basically saying:

“Insurance should be sold because customers need it, not simply because the distributor earns a lot by pushing it.”

The regulator wants to reduce excessive commissions, improve transparency and make insurance more affordable and sustainable.

💰 1. LOWER EXPENSE LIMITS

IRDAI is proposing tighter limits on how much insurers can spend.

For life insurers:

➡️ Around 15% of gross direct premium in 2 years

➡️ Around 12.5% in 5 years

➡️ Some already-efficient insurers could move toward 10%

For general insurers:

➡️ Around 20% in 5 years

In simple words:

Insurers may have less room to spend heavily on commissions, distribution and other expenses.

💸 2. COMMISSIONS COULD COME DOWN

This is the part the market is worried about most.

IRDAI wants to bring back product- and channel-specific commission limits.

Instead of paying a huge amount upfront for selling a policy, payouts could be:

➡️ Lower in the first year

➡️ Spread across the policy period

➡️ More closely linked to the actual effort/service involved

This could particularly affect:

🔹 Term insurance
🔹 Health insurance
🔹 Motor insurance
🔹 Credit-linked insurance

🏦 3. BIG CHANGE FOR BANKS & NBFCs

One proposal could have a major impact:

Banks/NBFCs would not be allowed to compulsorily bundle insurance with loans.

For example:

You take a ₹50 lakh loan.

The bank cannot effectively say:

“Take this insurance policy along with the loan.”

And credit-linked insurance commissions could become as low as 2–5% in some cases.

That is potentially a big change from the economics of these products today.

🚨 4. MIS-SELLING WILL GET MORE EXPENSIVE

IRDAI also wants:

✅ Stronger anti-mis-selling rules
✅ Commission clawbacks
✅ More disclosure of commissions on large policies
✅ Restrictions on “dark patterns”
✅ Less volume-based pressure on bank employees
✅ Simpler distributor categories

The broad idea:

Sell the right insurance to the customer, not simply the product that pays the most commission.

📉 SO WHY DID INSURANCE STOCKS FALL?

Because the market immediately started calculating:

“If commissions fall → distributor income falls → earnings could fall.”

🔴 Insurance distributors

Stocks such as PB Fintech (Policybazaar) and Turtlemint were among the more heavily impacted.

Their business models are closely connected to insurance distribution economics.

Some analysts estimated that even a 10% reduction in commissions could have a meaningful impact on earnings, depending on the company’s product mix.

🔴 Insurance companies

Several life and general insurers also fell, including names such as:

HDFC Life
ICICI Prudential Life
Max Financial
SBI Life
Star Health
ICICI Lombard
LIC

Why?

Because lower expense limits + lower upfront commissions could affect:

➡️ Distribution costs
➡️ New business growth
➡️ Margins
➡️ Incentives to sell certain products

🔴 Banks & NBFCs

Banks and lenders also came under pressure.

Why?

Because bancassurance and credit-linked insurance generate fee income.

If commissions on these products are sharply reduced and compulsory bundling is restricted that income stream could be affected.

Policybazaar Shares Fall 26% on IRDAI Proposals

Policybazaar parent PB Fintech shares came under heavy selling pressure, falling around 26%, after IRDAI proposed a wide-ranging overhaul of insurance distribution economics.

Proposed Changes to Insurance Commissions:
IRDAI's consultation paper proposes linking distributor commissions to factors including product complexity, distribution channel, policy size and selling effort.
For health insurance, the proposal includes commission limits of 15%–20% for new policies, while renewal and portability commissions could be capped at lower levels. Motor and life insurance commissions would also face proposed product-specific limits.

Why Policybazaar Is in Focus:
Policybazaar operates primarily as an online insurance distribution platform, making the proposed commission framework particularly relevant to its business economics.
According to Jefferies, a 10% reduction in commission rates could potentially translate into a 10%–12% decline in earnings for PB Fintech and Turtlemint. This is a brokerage estimate, not a confirmed impact.

IRDAI Also Targets Distribution Costs:
The regulator has proposed a five-year reduction in Expense of Management limits, alongside greater disclosure of commission structures and stronger safeguards against mis-selling.

The proposals also include restrictions on volume-linked incentives, commission clawbacks in cases of mis-selling, and greater use of digital infrastructure such as Bima Sugam.

The consultation process is currently open, with stakeholders invited to submit comments by October 25, 2026. These are proposals and are not yet final regulations.
